passage: Minakshi found a yellowed school report in the steel trunk at her mother's flat in Kolkata. Bhavna had been first in class at eleven, and a pencil note said, "Withdrawn, family needs." Minakshi read it standing in the hallway and thought of the years of sharp words about wasted rupees and the marks-or-nothing rule. Something in her softened, and sadness came with it. "Ma, you never went back to school, did you?" "No time," Bhavna said, taking the paper gently. Minakshi sat beside her and said nothing for a while. She did not say the past was fine. But that evening, when Bhavna began to raise her voice about the wedding budget, Minakshi said kindly, "Ma, I will talk when we can both be calm," and ended the call softly.

qa.q: What did the pencil note on the school report say?
What was Minakshi feeling in the hallway?
qa.a: Something softened in her, with sadness, as she began to see where her mother's harshness might have come from.

qa.q: How did Minakshi keep a boundary while feeling compassion?
qa.a: She said she would talk when both could be calm and ended the call softly.

qa.q: How might Bhavna have felt when Minakshi read the report?
qa.a: Bhavna took the paper gently and said there had been no time, which suggests an old loss she does not dwell on.

grounding: The protagonist sees a parent's harshness came from pain and poverty, feels sadness and softness, and still holds a boundary.

passage:
Thursday night.

Swati aunty, Ammi's old neighbour from Bhiwandi, came for lunch today. When Ammi went to the kitchen, she told me something I never knew. At eleven, Ammi was already cleaning houses. Her father drank. She was hit if the floors weren't shiny.

I sat there with my tea going cold.

All my life Ammi has been sharp. If my dupatta was crooked, she'd slap the back of my head. If I cried, she'd say, "Stop your drama." I've been angry with her for years.

Tonight I'm not less angry exactly. I'm sad. For her at eleven, scrubbing someone's floor with nobody to protect her. It made me softer, somehow.

But understanding isn't excusing. When I have children, I'll never hit them. And with Ammi, I'll be kind, and still leave the room when she starts shouting.

I'm Zainab. I'm her daughter, and I don't have to become her.

qa.q: At what age was Ammi already cleaning houses?
qa.a: She was cleaning houses at eleven.

qa.q: How did Zainab feel after hearing Swati aunty's story?
qa.a: Zainab felt sad and softer toward Ammi, though not less hurt.

qa.q: How does Zainab hold compassion and boundaries together?
qa.a: She plans to be kind to Ammi but still leave the room when she shouts, and to never hit her own children.

qa.q: How might Swati aunty have felt sharing Ammi's past?
qa.a: Swati aunty may have felt protective of Ammi and wanted Zainab to understand where her harshness came from.

grounding: A diary entry shows a young woman who learns her mother's harshness came from her own childhood pain and poverty, who feels sad and softer, understands without excusing and keeps boundaries.

passage:
Chetan: Gargi, you awake?
Gargi: yes. what's wrong
Chetan: Dada told me something tonight. about Papa
Chetan: when Papa was 14, Dadaji lost his job. Papa left school and worked at a garage for four years
Chetan: he never got to finish. that's why he screamed at us about marks. every single test
Gargi: oh
Gargi: I didn't know any of that
Chetan: me neither. I've been so angry at him for so long. now I just feel sad
Gargi: yeah. I feel sad too
Chetan: but I still remember him tearing up my drawings
Gargi: both can be true, bhai
Chetan: I don't want to excuse it. I don't want to do that to my kids either
Gargi: you won't. you already don't yell at Dhruv
Chetan: I'm going to call Papa on Sunday. just talk. but if he starts on my job again I'll hang up politely
Gargi: that sounds right
Chetan: thanks for listening

qa.q: Where did Papa work after leaving school?
qa.a: He worked at a garage for four years.

qa.q: How did Chetan feel after learning about Papa's past?
qa.a: Chetan felt sad and softer toward Papa, after years of anger.

qa.q: How does Chetan plan to be kind without excusing the past?
qa.a: He will call Papa on Sunday to talk but hang up politely if Papa starts criticising, and he won't repeat the yelling with his own children.

qa.q: How does Gargi respond to Chetan's feelings?
qa.a: Gargi shares the sadness and reminds him that both the pain and the understanding can be true.

grounding: A chat shows a young man who learns his father's harshness came from his own poverty and pain, who feels sad and softer while keeping boundaries and not repeating the pattern.
